_about: The facts THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md states that no README of this repository holds: the licences of the libraries the page loads from a CDN, the hosts the site's code names, the helper tools and packages, and the wording of the catalogue and YouTube sections. They are G13 section E8's facts (measured 2026-10-08) and nothing is guessed: a tool whose licence this repository does not state says 'see the project's own licence'. tools/notices/build.js reads this file with vendor/README.md, audio/piano/README.md, catalog/*/README.md and catalog/*/index.json; tests/notices/notices.test.js keeps it in step with the page.

cdn._about: Packages the served code (the page, support.js and the modules it loads) names at cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm, unpkg.com or esm.sh. Every package found there must have a row here, and a row whose package is no longer named (it was vendored) must go: build.js --check says which.

@babel/standalone.name: Babel standalone
@babel/standalone.use: named by support.js for JSX templates; this page has none and never requests it

fallbackOf._about: npm packages that PPP serves itself (vendor/) and that the page names at a CDN only as the way back (?cdn=1, or when PPP's own copy cannot be fetched). They need no row of their own here: the section of vendor/README.md is theirs.

fonts._about: Families of the Google Fonts stylesheets the page asks for after it has loaded, and only on a device that has no font of its own for the script (Korean, Japanese and Chinese text; G13-4b2): the Latin families are served by PPP itself (vendor/fonts).

other.name: Onsets and Frames checkpoint (Magenta model weights)
other.use: the in-browser recording transcription; about 60 MB, fetched only when a recording is converted in the browser
other.licence: see the checkpoint's own terms (this repository does not restate them)

hosts._about: Every http(s) host the served code names (the page, support.js and the modules static-allow.js hands out, comments cut out) must be here, with what it is. A host that carries a library, a font or data (npm, fonts, storage) is covered by the rows of 'cdn' above and must still be named by the code; a service is listed in the notices; a link is something the page sends a person to or shares to (nothing is loaded from it); a namespace is an XML/SVG identifier. A new host that is not here fails build.js --check: say what it is first, and give a licence row if it loads anything.

service.www.youtube-nocookie.com: the video player shown beside a song that has a YouTube video (YouTube's own embed)
service.www.youtube.com: the title of a video (oEmbed) when PPP's own server cannot give it, and links to the video

own.text: `support.js` is the runtime of the page, generated for PPP. It carries no licence header and the source it is generated from is not in this repository.

helpers._about: Software, models and packages that run on your own computer or on the server, not in the page. A licence is given only where this repository states it, and `evidence` names the file and the words that say so (build.js --check reads them); every other row says 'see the project's own licence'. `ids` are what the pinned requirements (requirements-*.txt), the models of the setup scripts (tools/home-worker/setup-*.cmd) and the runtime dependencies of package.json are matched against: one that has no row here and no omission fails the check.

catalogue._about: How a catalogue licence code of catalog/method/index.json reads in the notices file; and which pieces are marked 'under review' in its table (tests/notices/notices.test.js checks them against the benchmark's provenance record).
catalogue.underReviewText: The compositions are in the public domain. Czerny 40 (all 10 pieces) and Burgmüller 25 nos. 1, 2, 4, 7 and 18 are community typesets whose files carry no public-domain or CC0 statement of their own: the dataset lists them as CC0, and the piece-level statement is under review.

demo.text: The score that opens first is a practice pattern generated by PPP (`buildDemoScore` in the page). Its title names a film piece and its composer, but its notes are not that piece's melody, and the composer has no connection with PPP.

youtube.text: When you paste a YouTube link, PPP fetches that video's audio (on the server, or on your own PC when you use the PC worker) only to write the notes it hears; the audio is not kept on the server. If YouTube refuses the server, the server falls back to a third-party download site (loader.to), which then receives the link you pasted. Your browser also contacts YouTube to show the video (the youtube-nocookie.com player) and, when PPP's server cannot, to look up its title (oEmbed). Use recordings you have the right to use. The score PPP writes is for your own practice: a score made from a YouTube link cannot be posted to Shared Scores, although you can still send its link.
